subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: The live_preview config uses `management_token` instead of the prescribed `preview_token`. The Root Cause Analysis explicitly prescribes `live_preview: { enable: true, preview_token: process.env.CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN || '' }`. The `contentstack` delivery SDK's live_preview block expects `preview_token` for preview-mode detection; `management_token` is a Contentstack Management API concept, not a delivery SDK config key. Using the wrong key means the SDK will not detect preview mode and will never return draft entries — live preview will silently not work. Additionally, the `|| ''` fallback from the plan is omitted, so when CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN is unset the value is a raw empty string without the defensive coalesce.
issues.suggestedFix: Change `management_token: CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN` to `preview_token: CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN || ''` as prescribed. Remove the `host` field unless the SDK documentation explicitly requires it for preview (the plan does not mention it).

issues.description: Hardcoded endpoint URL `host: "api.contentstack.io"` violates the project rule: no hardcoded strings for endpoint URLs — all must use named constants from src/config/constants.ts. This host is also not part of the prescribed fix and may be incorrect for the preview API endpoint.
issues.suggestedFix: If a host override is genuinely needed, add a named constant (e.g., CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST) to src/config/constants.ts sourced from an environment variable. Otherwise, remove the `host` field entirely and let the SDK use its default.

issues.description: Importing `getSinglePageEntry` from `services/pageService.ts` pulls the entire pageService module and its full dependency tree (contactUsService, newsService, podcastService, projectsSearchService, regionService, topicService, mappers, utils/fsCache, etc.) into the client-side bundle. The plan prescribes using `getSingleEntry` from `services/contentstack.ts` directly with the same contentstackConfig lookup pattern that getSinglePageEntry uses (lines 75-88 of pageService.ts). contentstack.ts is already imported client-side (for `Stack`) and has a much smaller dependency footprint.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the `getSinglePageEntry` import with `getSingleEntry` from `services/contentstack.ts` and `contentstackConfig` from `constants/contentstack`. Inline the 3-line config lookup: `const config = contentstackConfig[contentTypeUid]; const page = await getSingleEntry({ contentTypeUid, entryUid, lang, ...config });`. Remove the `export` added to `getSinglePageEntry` in pageService.ts.

issues.description: The `setContent` field added to `IContentstackContext` is never populated in the provider value. The implementation manages reactive state via `useState` in _app.tsx and passes the value directly to `ContentstackContext.Provider`, so `setContent` is dead code. Any consumer calling `context.setContent(...)` would get `undefined` and crash at runtime.
issues.suggestedFix: Either remove `setContent` from the interface (the useState + Provider value pattern already achieves reactivity), or wire it: include `setContent: setPage` in the provider value so the interface contract is fulfilled.

issues.description: The `.catch(() => {})` block silently swallows all preview re-fetch errors with no logging. While falling back to published content is the correct behavior, silently swallowing errors makes debugging live preview issues impossible in production.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a minimal logger call: `.catch((e) => { console.warn('Live preview re-fetch failed, falling back to published content:', e); })` or use the project's logger service.

issues.description: The useEffect dependency array `[pageProps, routerLocale]` causes `ContentstackLivePreview.init()` to be called on every route change / pageProps update. Repeated init() calls may cause the SDK to register duplicate onEntryChange listeners or leak resources, depending on the SDK's idempotency guarantees.
issues.suggestedFix: Split into two effects: one with `[]` dependencies for `ContentstackLivePreview.init()` (run once), and one with `[pageProps, routerLocale]` for the `onEntryChange` callback registration. Alternatively, guard init with a ref flag to ensure it runs only once.

issues.description: SPEC: The acceptance criteria require that when a draft entry change is signaled while the page is in a protected or gated state, the page does not render draft content. The plan's prescribed fix does not address this criterion — there is no gated-state check in the onEntryChange callback. This is a gap in the plan of record, not a failure by the implementer. The onEntryChange callback unconditionally calls setPage with the re-fetched entry regardless of page protection state.
issues.suggestedFix: SPEC advisory: The plan should be amended to include a guard in the onEntryChange callback that checks whether the current page is in a protected/gated state (e.g., via session/auth state) and skips the draft update if so. The implementer should not be expected to implement this without plan guidance.

subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: The new app-level ContentstackContext.Provider is shadowed by the existing per-page providers, so draft content can never reach any consumer. The actual page content is rendered under pages/[[...slug]].tsx line 39 (`<ContentstackContext.Provider value={content}>`) and pages/404.tsx line 31, both of which set the context from static server-fetched props. Every real consumer (Homepage, Header, Layout, and the 147+ useContent consumers) reads from THAT inner provider, not the new one in _app.tsx. When onEntryChange fires, setPage updates only the outer app-level context value — the inner provider's `value={content}` is unchanged, so nothing the user sees re-renders with draft data. This fails every verification criterion that requires the rendered page to show the draft entry. Additionally, `pageProps.contentstackContext` (used to seed the state at line 73) is never produced by any getStaticProps — the slug page returns `content` and `contentTypeUid` only — so the app-level context starts as `{}` in production. The prescribed fix required the provider that actually feeds useContent consumers to carry the reactive state; this implements a parallel provider that feeds nobody.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the provider of record reactive: in pages/[[...slug]].tsx (the component that owns `<ContentstackContext.Provider value={content}>`), hold `page` in state seeded from `content.page` and update it from the onEntryChange callback, so the provider value that Homepage and all useContent consumers read is the one that changes. The setPage/onEntryChange wiring can stay in _app.tsx only if the updated entry is passed down so it overrides the page-level provider value (e.g., via a page-props-independent channel the slug page consumes). Verify end-to-end that after onEntryChange, the value read by useContent inside the rendered page reflects the draft entry.

issues.description: The onEntryChange re-fetch never executes for the pages in scope. The guard `if (!contentTypeUid || !entryUid) return;` destructures both values from pageProps, but pages/[[...slug]].tsx getStaticProps returns only `content`, `contentTypeUid`, and translations — there is no `entryUid` prop. For the MX Homepage and Discover Article pages (both served through the catch-all slug route), `entryUid` is always undefined, the callback exits silently, and no draft re-fetch is ever issued even when a live preview hash is active. Combined with the shadowed-provider issue, the feature is doubly inert on its target pages.
issues.suggestedFix: Derive the entry UID from data that actually exists in pageProps — e.g. `(pageProps as { content?: { page?: [IContentstackPage] } }).content?.page?.[0]?.uid` — or add `entryUid` to the props returned by the slug route's getStaticProps, so the guard passes for Homepage and Discover Article pages.

issues.description: The useEffect registering ContentstackLivePreview.onEntryChange depends on [pageProps, routerLocale], so the callback is re-registered on every navigation and props change. If the util accumulates (rather than replaces) subscribers, each entry change will fire N stale callbacks — duplicate re-fetches racing each other — which jeopardises the criterion that successive draft changes render in sequence. If it replaces, earlier closures capturing stale pageProps are fine only by accident.
issues.suggestedFix: Register onEntryChange once (empty dependency array, alongside the init effect) and read the latest contentTypeUid/entryUid/locale inside the callback via a ref, so exactly one fetch is issued per entry change.

issues.description: `host: CONTENTSTACK_LIVE_PREVIEW_HOST` defaults to an empty string when the env var is unset. The SDK's built-in default live_preview host is 'api.contentstack.io' (visible in the SDK's default config), but passing an explicit empty string overrides that default, so in any environment missing CONTENTSTACK_LIVE_PREVIEW_HOST the preview re-fetch targets an invalid host and fails — a silent regression-by-config. The plan prescribed only enable + token; the host was added without a fallback.
issues.suggestedFix: Default to the SDK's host: `host: CONTENTSTACK_LIVE_PREVIEW_HOST || 'api.contentstack.io'` (via a named constant), or omit `host` entirely when the env var is unset so the SDK default applies.

issues.description: `getContentByKey<[IContentstackPage] | undefined>('page', undefined);` discards its return value and subscribes to nothing — useContent's useContext already makes the component a context consumer, so the call is a no-op whose comment ('Subscribe to the reactive page entry') misdescribes it. It is also an unused expression likely to trip @typescript-eslint/no-unused-expressions, and the surrounding LivePreviewPage wrapper (~25 lines) currently exists only to re-render children with unchanged pageProps (it cannot propagate the draft past the page-level provider — see blocker 1).
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the no-op getContentByKey call; once blocker 1 is fixed by making the page-level provider reactive, the entire LivePreviewPage wrapper is unnecessary — restore the original `<Component {...pageProps} key={path} />` for a smaller diff.

issues.description: `IContentstackPageProps` declares a `page?: [IContentstackPage]` field that is never read anywhere in the file; only contentTypeUid and entryUid are destructured. Dead interface surface.
issues.suggestedFix: Drop the unused `page` field (and the IContentstackPage import if it becomes unused) from IContentstackPageProps.
